g.text: The identity adjustment now holds in two independent
cohorts under a rule fixed before the second was acquired:

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 6.3px; font-family: 'Liberation Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #898781

g.text: It is not causal, and one gene helps it.
These are cross-sectional transcriptomes. AIFM2 is
absent from HG-U133A, so GSE14520's REDUCTION is a 3-gene
score — and AIFM2 ran opposite to its module in PHASE B.

font-weight: 700; font-size: 10px; font-family: 'Liberation Sans'; text-anchor: start

g.text: Cohorts, covariate and decision rule fixed in PREREGISTRATION §6h before any replication number existed; §6i records the completion of
GSE14520's acquisition, including the recovery of HNF1A from its retired symbol TCF1, before any adjusted number was computed. GSE164760
returns "uninformative" by that rule because its unadjusted DRAIN shift is absent, and is counted as neither support nor refutation. D2 adds the
hepatic P450s to the covariate and is expected to over-adjust, because POR donates electrons to those very enzymes.
